editorial:
Ever wonder who actually picked the hits that played on every radio for decades? You get to step inside the mind of Clive Davis, the man who turned singers into superstars. It feels less like a dry history lesson and more like a backstage pass to the music industry. You will see how he started at Columbia Records and later built Arista, all while dealing with huge egos and massive risks. The vibe is polished and inspiring, filled with great stories about how the songs you love actually came to be.

What really makes this work is the sheer amount of music and the interviews with legends who actually worked with him. The pacing is smooth, though it can feel a bit like a highlight reel since it covers so many years. If you love music history, you should definitely check this out. It is a great pick for a lazy Sunday afternoon.
endingExplained: The movie wraps up by looking at Clive's lasting impact on the music world. It shows him reflecting on his journey from a young executive to a legendary mogul. Instead of a big twist, it ends with a celebration of his career and the artists he helped create. You see a final montage of his biggest hits, leaving you with the feeling that his ear for talent changed pop music forever.
targetAudience: Ideal for anyone who loves music history and behind-the-scenes stories.
